set.body:
Split out of P8.D6, whose completion note wrongly claimed this was already done.

modules/core/.../SharedKernel.scala declares ~20 PACKAGE-LEVEL aliases in io.github.bbuchsbaum.slurm4s.core:

    type SubmissionKey = io.github.bbuchsbaum.remoteexec.kernel.SubmissionKey
    val SubmissionKey = io.github.bbuchsbaum.remoteexec.kernel.SubmissionKey

Because they are package-level, every `import ...slurm4s.core.*` resolves these names through this file without ever mentioning SharedKernel. Grepping for the identifier finds nothing, which is what produced the wrong conclusion in D6. Measured: deleting the file yields 610 compile errors in core alone.

ADR 0010 anticipates the removal — "these pre-1.0 aliases carry no independent semantics and may be removed after downstream migration" — but the migration itself has not happened.

The work: every consumer currently receiving ValidationFailure, SubmissionKey, AttemptId, OperationId, OperationVersion, OperationDescriptor and the rest via core.* must import io.github.bbuchsbaum.remoteexec.kernel explicitly, then the file goes.

SEQUENCING: do this BEFORE P7.6 cuts the compatibility baseline. It changes the public import surface of slurm4s-core, so cutting a baseline first would publish a surface intended for removal and then break it.

Also worth deciding as part of this: whether slurm4s-core should re-export kernel types deliberately (a curated facade, documented as such) rather than removing the aliases outright. ADR 0010 assumed removal; a downstream consumer who has to import two packages to name one identifier may disagree. That is a design call, not a cleanup.
set.title: P8.D6b: Migrate off the SharedKernel package-level aliases
